root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward sharpness, cutting edges, and forceful keenness.
root_idea.development: The sharpness principle appears physically in sawing wood and serrated edges, and figuratively in energetic impetuosity and excessive exultation.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied Quranic group is an adjectival form and is presented under its normalized masculine singular citation form.

senses.definition: Extremely exultant, insolent, boastful, and unthankful.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic adjective for exultation driven by pride and desire rather than a rightly directed joy; the term is stronger than ordinary بَطَرٌ, or self-delighting exultation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To divide or saw a piece of wood with a saw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use concerning cutting wood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make teeth serrated and sharpen their tips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tooth-sharpening and serration practice; the source illustrates it with making the teeth resemble those of a young person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To invite another to have the teeth serrated and their tips sharpened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived construction referring to arranging or requesting the tooth-sharpening practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of lightning: flashing repeatedly to and fro.
Of a plant or herbage: extending beyond its proper bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use describing excessive outward growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Serrations or sharp projections at the ends of teeth; by extension, the teeth of a reaping hook or sickle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe natural or artificial tooth serration and is also applied to serrated cutting projections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In أُمْنِيَّةٌ أَشْرَاءُ, an intensely exultant or overweening wish.
One who divides or saws wood with a saw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial noun for the wood-sawing activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Serrated projections on a locust’s shanks and claw-like projections at the end of its tail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical application associated with serrated or cutting projections.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who has the ends of her teeth sharpened and serrated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine agent noun for the tooth-sharpening practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In يَدٌ آشِرَةٌ, a hand or arm that has been sawn off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression in which the active-looking adjective has a passive resultative sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thing with which a locust bites.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun; its plural is also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Made thin and serrated; especially a tooth sharpened at its tip or a similarly serrated part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to sharpened front teeth and to thin, serrated fore-shanks of a beetle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A saw, an instrument for dividing wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool noun with recorded plural مَآشِيرُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wood divided or sawn with a saw.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial noun describing the resulting wood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman whose tooth tips have been sharpened and serrated artificially.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine passive participial noun for the result of the tooth-sharpening practice.
Applied to people and animals, without restriction to one sex.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who invites another to have the teeth serrated and their tips sharpened.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine derived participial use referring to the tooth-sharpening construction.

cautions: The two Quranic occurrences attest the adjectival exultation and insolence branch; the sawing, serration, anatomical, and liveliness branches are broader Classical Arabic evidence.

The Arabic labels for the locust-related subunits of Lane entry 6798 are partially lost in the supplied transcription; their anatomical referents are clear, but the exact subheadword labeling is uncertain.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The omitted Arabic terms in lane-unit:A$r:6798:g1:sub2 and lane-unit:A$r:6798:g1:sub3 prevent certainty about the precise lexical labels attached to the locust shank and tail projections, although the meanings are represented under آشِرٌ.
